posts.title: Another Joseph Epstein essay: Turning 90
posts.description: Joseph Epstein insightfully recounts his experiences with growing old, in an essay preceding his 90th birthday in January. Read it in Commentary here . "While I am grateful to be arriving at 90, life now seems less amusing. More and more, it seems about loss, loss both personal and of so many of the things that made life interesting and often amusing. The loss of friends, to begin with. . . ."

posts.title: Why Am I So Negative About Traditional Book Publishing? by Dean Wesley Smith
posts.description: "Traditional book publishing with thousands of publishers worked pretty well from 1960 to 1995 and then it just fell apart. Those good years are where the myths built up. Now in the last 30 years, traditional publishing and its four publishers has become a sad little echo of the thousands of publishers that came before." Full article here . One of the commentators to the above post (Steve Perry) wrote: "Trad-pub peaked, I think, just before the Great Recession of 2007-2009, that took with it the traditional publishing midlist and the careers of a shitload of writers." I have to join in and say this entirely mirrors my own experience. The midlist (the place for quirky interesting books, often nonfiction) started dying around 1995, when all the mainstream publishing went fishing for potential bestsellers, leaving everything else behind.
